hypothesis: For a mid-market B2B SaaS support operation, routing a subset of incoming tickets through a governed multi-agent support workflow (triage, resolver, knowledge, and quality-review agents) will reduce average handle time and cost per ticket by at least 25% while maintaining or improving first-contact resolution rate and CSAT, compared with a human-only tiered queue, under equivalent ticket mix and operating hours.

baseline.description: Current human-only customer support operation using standard tiered queues (Tier 1 / Tier 2) across email and chat, integrated with a ticketing system (e.g., Zendesk, Freshdesk, or a synthetic equivalent).

channels: In-app chat widget (synchronous where possible, async fallback)
queue_design.routing_logic: All tickets land in a single Level 1 (L1) inbox. L1 agents manually triage, respond, and either resolve or escalate to Level 2 (L2) based on perceived complexity and permissions.

tiers.name: Tier 1 (L1)
tiers.permissions: Read/write to tickets, access to KB, limited account changes, no billing changes.
tiers.operating_hours: Business hours coverage (e.g., 9am–6pm in target time zone).

tiers.name: Tier 2 (L2)
tiers.permissions: All L1 permissions plus advanced account configuration, API troubleshooting, and limited billing adjustments.
tiers.operating_hours: Same as L1 for this experiment; off-hours tickets are queued.

steps: Customer submits ticket via email/chat/web form.
Ticketing system creates a ticket with metadata (channel, timestamp, customer ID, subject, body).
L1 agent manually picks ticket from the queue.
Agent reads context (recent tickets, CRM info) and categorizes the ticket (issue type, priority, product area) using dropdowns in the ticketing UI.
Agent searches internal knowledge base or prior tickets as needed.
Agent writes a free-form response, optionally inserting macros or templates.
If unable to resolve, agent escalates the ticket to L2 or another team with internal comments.
Ticket is resolved and closed by human agents; optionally a CSAT survey is triggered on closure.

guardrails.tone_guidelines: Human agents trained to follow written support style guidelines (professional, concise, empathetic).
guardrails.policy_compliance: Relies on human training, occasional QA review, and manager spot-checks; no systematic automated policy enforcement.
guardrails.escalation_criteria: Informal or defined in playbooks, but applied inconsistently; documented only in SOPs.

baseline_metrics_collection.period: Minimum 4 weeks of historical data prior to experiment, or synthetic rerun of historical tickets through human-only queues.
required_events: Each status change (open, pending, on-hold, solved/closed)
Any refunds/credits or policy-relevant actions taken

treatment.description: Agentic support queue in which incoming tickets are handled by a coordinated set of support agents (triage, resolver, knowledge, and quality-review) integrated with the same ticketing/CRM stack, with human supervisors handling escalations and spot-checks.

triage_agent.purpose: Classify, prioritize, and route tickets; detect spam; suggest immediate auto-responses when confidence is high.
inputs: Past ticket history for the customer
outputs: Routing decision: auto-resolve candidate vs. assign to resolver agent vs. escalate directly to human
Policy flags (potential abuse, legal risk, security issue)

knowledge_agent.purpose: Retrieve relevant KB articles, prior tickets, FAQ entries, and product docs via RAG to support resolution.

resolver_agent.purpose: Draft responses and resolution steps using KB context, propose ticket updates (status, tags), and recommend actions.
outputs: Draft reply to customer (structured: greeting, body, steps, closing)
Structured actions: labels, status change, suggested escalation, recommended macros
Confidence score and auto-send eligibility flag
constraints: Must not make irreversible account changes or financial promises; only propose them.
Must adhere to tone and policy templates enforced via system prompts and validation tools.

quality_review_agent.purpose: Check drafted responses for tone, policy compliance, safety, and correctness before auto-sending or surfacing to human.
checks: Prohibited phrases/policies (credits, refunds, SLAs) against configuration rules.
Hallucination guardrails (no unsupported claims; cross-checks with KB snippets).
outputs: Reject and request re-draft with reasons

steps: Ticket arrives in the system as in the baseline.
Integration service posts normalized ticket payload to an orchestration layer (e.g., via message queue or webhook).
Triage agent runs and assigns classification, priority, and routing decision.
a. Knowledge agent retrieves context from KB and historical tickets.
b. Resolver agent drafts a proposed reply and structured actions.
c. Quality-review agent validates the draft; if low risk and high confidence, auto-sends; otherwise, routes to human review inbox with suggested reply attached.
If triage detects high-risk categories (billing disputes, legal threats, security incidents), ticket is routed to human-only queue with agentic suggestions disabled or read-only.
All agent steps, intermediate outputs, and decisions are logged in an audit trail attached to the ticket.
Human supervisors can override, edit, or block agent actions; this feedback is logged and used for evaluation.

guardrails.tone: Enforced via both prompt instructions and a deterministic tone-checker (rule-based or LLM with strict schema) as part of quality-review.
guardrails.policy_compliance: Formalized policy rules encoded as machine-checkable constraints (e.g., no refunds above $X, no changes to contract terms, no data shared beyond configured fields).
guardrails.escalation_criteria: Explicit lists of topics and patterns (keywords, regexes, classifier tags) that force human review or direct escalation (e.g., 'breach', 'lawsuit', 'GDPR', 'HIPAA').

integration_changes.ticketing: Webhook or polling integration from the ticketing system into the orchestration API, plus status and comment update API calls back into tickets.
integration_changes.crm: Read-only access to basic customer attributes (plan, MRR, tenure, region). No PII beyond what is already visible to human agents.
integration_changes.email_chat: Agentic replies posted back via ticketing APIs; no direct SMTP/IM integration required if ticketing system already handles outbound messages.

workloads.name: historical_replay_workload
workloads.description: Offline replay of previously resolved tickets through both human-only (as-logged) and agentic workflows to compare outputs and simulate impact without affecting live customers.

data_source.option_a_real: Anonymized export of 10,000–50,000 historical tickets with full timelines from the production ticketing system.
data_source.option_b_synthetic: Synthetic generator that creates tickets for common issues (login, billing question, feature how-to, bug report, integration setup) based on a predefined taxonomy and seeded templates.

sampling.time_window: At least 4 consecutive weeks, excluding major incident periods if possible.
sampling.stratification: Stratify by channel (email/chat/web), customer segment (SMB/mid-market/enterprise), and main issue category to match real distribution.
sampling.holdout_sets: Reserve a 20% subset as a final evaluation set not used during configuration of prompts/guardrails.

workloads.execution_mode: Offline: for each ticket in the workload, reconstruct the initial state and run the agentic pipeline to propose responses and actions; compare against human final responses.
workloads.constraints: No outbound messages are sent to customers; this is a shadow run.

workloads.name: live_ab_workload
workloads.description: Online randomized controlled trial where new incoming tickets are randomly assigned to agentic vs. human-only handling under guardrails.

assignment.randomization_scheme: Bernoulli randomization at ticket creation time with configurable probability p for treatment (e.g., 0.3–0.5).
assignment.stratification: Optional stratification by channel and customer plan to ensure balance in key segments.

traffic_allocation.phase_1: 10% treatment, 90% control for 3–5 days to validate safety and guardrails.
traffic_allocation.phase_2: 30–50% treatment, 50–70% control for main measurement period (at least 2–4 weeks).
exclusions: High-risk categories always assigned to control or human-supervised agentic path.
VIP accounts can be excluded or kept at lower treatment fraction initially.

operational_constraints.business_hours: Initial experiment limited to staffed hours to ensure human escalations are promptly handled.
operational_constraints.max_auto_send: Cap fraction of treatment tickets that can receive auto-sent responses without human review (e.g., <= 40%) during early phases.

traffic_splitting.mechanism: Deterministic random assignment using ticket_id hash or an experiment service to avoid bias by agent selection.
invariance_checks: Compare pre-treatment ticket volume per channel between arms.
Compare distribution of categories, priorities, and customer segments across control and treatment.
Ensure no major incident or new product launch occurs disproportionately in one arm.

agent_configuration_freeze.description: Prompt templates, model versions, routing thresholds, and guardrail policies must be frozen at the start of the main measurement window.
agent_configuration_freeze.exceptions: Critical safety fixes are allowed but must be documented with timestamps and considered in analysis.

staffing_levels.description: Maintain equivalent or at least non-decreasing human staffing during the experiment relative to the baseline period.
staffing_levels.constraint: No intentional reduction in staff based solely on experimental treatment; otherwise results confound efficiency with staffing cuts.

training_and_change_management.human_agents: All participating human agents receive training on how to supervise the agentic queue, provide feedback, and escalate safely.
training_and_change_management.blinding: Agents need not be blinded to the experiment, but should not change process only for one arm; workflow differences must be enforced by the system, not ad hoc behavior.

logging_requirements: Arm assignment (control vs. treatment) stored with ticket.
Timestamps of all key events (creation, first response, each agent step, resolution).
Flags for human override, agent auto-reply, and agent suggestions that were rejected.
Customer satisfaction responses and any free-text survey comments.
data_collection.privacy: All logs must exclude or anonymize PII before export to the analysis environment.

metrics.name: avg_first_response_time
metrics.definition: Mean duration from ticket creation to first customer-visible reply (human or agent) within the experiment window.
metrics.scope: Per arm (control vs. treatment), with breakdowns by channel and priority.

metrics.name: avg_handle_time_per_ticket
metrics.definition: Mean total active handling time per ticket, including sum of all human work intervals plus estimated agent computation time converted into human-equivalent labor minutes.
metrics.scope: Per arm; excludes waiting time between replies.

metrics.name: first_contact_resolution_rate
metrics.definition: Proportion of tickets resolved without requiring a second separate interaction after the first substantive response, excluding automated acknowledgments.
metrics.scope: Per arm; computed as tickets closed within a configured window (e.g., 48 hours) with exactly one customer-facing response thread.

metrics.name: csat_score
metrics.definition: Average CSAT score from post-resolution surveys on a 1–5 or 1–10 scale, normalized to a 0–100 index if necessary.
metrics.scope: Per arm; include response rate as a supplementary diagnostic metric.

metrics.name: nps_score
metrics.definition: Net Promoter Score from periodic or transactionally-triggered surveys associated with support interactions.
metrics.scope: Optional if NPS is available at the interaction level; otherwise limited to CSAT.

metrics.name: cost_per_ticket
metrics.definition: Total operational cost divided by the number of tickets, including allocated human labor cost and incremental agent/infra cost.
components: Human cost: (Total human handling time in hours * blended hourly fully loaded rate) / tickets.
Agentic cost: LLM/API charges, vector DB queries, orchestration infra, allocated proportionally per ticket.

metrics.name: escalation_rate_to_human
metrics.definition: In treatment arm, proportion of tickets initially handled by agents that require human intervention (review, override, or takeover).
metrics.scope: Treatment only; used as an indicator of agent coverage and complexity.

metrics.name: policy_violation_incidents
metrics.definition: Confirmed cases where replies or actions violated predefined policy constraints (credits/refunds, security disclosures, compliance rules), as determined by QA audits.

metrics.name: auto_resolution_rate
metrics.definition: In treatment arm, fraction of tickets resolved without any human edits to the agent-proposed response.
metrics.scope: Treatment only; stratified by issue category and channel.

metrics.name: agent_suggestion_acceptance_rate
metrics.definition: For tickets where agents propose draft replies to humans, proportion of suggestions that are accepted with minor or no edits.
metrics.scope: Treatment only; indicates quality of agent assistance.

primary.target: >= 25% reduction in treatment vs. control, with 95% confidence interval excluding 0% reduction.
primary.rationale: Aligns with chapter goal of demonstrating material economic improvement while maintaining quality.

primary.target: Non-inferior (no statistically significant decrease greater than 2 percentage points) in treatment vs. control.
primary.rationale: Ensures that efficiency gains do not come at the cost of more back-and-forth or unresolved tickets.

primary.target: Non-inferior with a pre-specified non-inferiority margin (e.g., <= 2 points decrease on a 0–100 normalized scale), or improved.

secondary.rationale: Operational efficiency indicator; often the primary driver of human cost savings.

secondary.target: >= 20% reduction in treatment vs. control, subject to staffing parity.
No statistically significant increase; ideally reduction due to automated guardrails.
At least 20% of low-complexity tickets (e.g., password reset, simple FAQ) fully handled by agents with no human edits.
secondary.rationale: Demonstrates meaningful automation coverage in well-defined slices.

statistical_considerations.minimum_sample_size_estimate: Dependent on baseline variance; as a starting point, at least 5,000 tickets per arm for robust inference in a mid-market B2B SaaS context.
statistical_considerations.analysis_plan_summary: Use two-sample t-tests or non-parametric equivalents for continuous metrics (handle time, cost), and chi-squared or proportion tests for rates (FCR, CSAT, policy violations), adjusting for multiple comparisons where appropriate.

failure_modes.name: distribution_shift_between_arms
failure_modes.description: Ticket mix (issues, segments, incident periods) differs substantially between control and treatment, invalidating comparisons.
mitigations: Run pre-experiment invariance checks on early randomized data.
Stratify analysis by key segments (issue category, channel, customer tier).
Optionally re-weight observations to match distributions.

failure_modes.name: guardrail_bypass_or_misconfiguration
failure_modes.description: Agentic replies violate policy because escalation or pattern checks are too permissive or incorrectly encoded.
mitigations: Shadow-mode dry run of guardrails using historical tickets before enabling auto-send.
Limit auto-send to low-risk categories during early phases.
Require human review for any ticket hitting sensitive keywords or high-risk categories.

failure_modes.name: human_behavior_change_bias
failure_modes.description: Human agents behave differently when supervising agentic suggestions (e.g., more careful or careless) than in pure manual mode, confounding comparisons.
mitigations: Train agents to follow consistent review policies.
Use clear UI cues and workflows to limit differences besides agent assistance.
Measure human editing effort and incorporate into cost and handle time estimates.

failure_modes.name: measurement_inaccuracy_in_handle_time
failure_modes.description: Ticket system logs do not fully capture true human time spent per ticket, especially for multitasking and context switching.
mitigations: Use a combination of ticket events (assignment, status changes) and sampling-based time tracking to calibrate estimates.
Apply consistent estimation methods to both arms.
Report sensitivity analyses using alternative handle time approximations.

failure_modes.name: model_regressions_or_api_instability
failure_modes.description: LLM service changes behavior or experiences outages during the experiment, distorting results or harming customer experience.
mitigations: Implement automatic fallback to human-only handling in case of repeated agent failures or timeouts.
Log all agent errors and treat affected tickets as separate in analysis.

failure_modes.name: overfitting_to_historical_data
failure_modes.description: Prompts and guardrails tuned too specifically to historical replay workloads may not generalize to live traffic.
mitigations: Reserve a holdout set of historical tickets not used during tuning.
Run a small but diverse live pilot (10% treatment) before scaling.
Continuously monitor error types and adjust policies cautiously.

infrastructure.runtime: Python 3.10+ environment (or equivalent) with access to LLM APIs, vector database, and ticketing/CRM APIs.
infrastructure.deployment: Containerized services (e.g., Docker, Kubernetes) or serverless functions for agent orchestration and integrations.
infrastructure.data_store: Relational database for experiment logs and analytics (e.g., PostgreSQL), plus a vector store (e.g., PostgreSQL with pgvector, Pinecone, Weaviate, or similar) for KB embeddings.
infrastructure.messaging: Queue or pub/sub system (e.g., RabbitMQ, Kafka, AWS SQS/SNS) to decouple ticket events from agent processing.
infrastructure.monitoring: Basic observability stack (logs, metrics, dashboards) such as Prometheus/Grafana or a SaaS equivalent.

dependencies.llm_provider: Access to at least one modern LLM with function-calling / tool-use capabilities via API (e.g., OpenAI, Anthropic, Azure OpenAI).
dependencies.ticketing_system: Sandbox or production instance with API access (e.g., Zendesk Support, Freshdesk, Intercom, or synthetic in-repo implementation).
dependencies.crm_system: Sandbox or synthetic CRM (e.g., HubSpot, Salesforce, or a simple Postgres-backed mock) with read-only API access for customer profiles.
dependencies.kb_system: Knowledge base exported as markdown, HTML, or JSON to be indexed in vector DB; can also be a synthetic KB included in the repository.

security_and_compliance.data_protection: Anonymization or pseudonymization of PII when exporting logs for analysis.
security_and_compliance.access_controls: Least-privilege API tokens for agents; read-only wherever possible; no direct database write access except through audited services.
security_and_compliance.audit_logging: All agent tool calls and decisions logged with timestamps, input hashes, and outputs.

configuration.experiment_flags: Feature flags or configuration toggles to route tickets to control or treatment paths based on assignment.
configuration.policy_files: Machine-readable policy configuration (YAML/JSON) defining high-risk categories, red-flag keywords, and allowed actions.
configuration.prompt_templates: Version-controlled prompt files for each agent role, stored in the repository with appropriate redaction of secrets.

run_instructions.overview: Run the experiment in two phases: (1) offline historical replay for tuning and safety verification; (2) live A/B test for operational and business impact, with phased rollout and monitoring.

step_by_step.title: Set up repository and environment
actions: Clone the book's companion repository: git clone https://github.com/bookauthority/turn-your-company-into-an-agentic-organization.git
Navigate to the customer support experiment directory (e.g., experiments/ch08_cx_agentic_support).
Create and activate a Python virtual environment.
Install dependencies from requirements.txt or pyproject.toml.
Configure environment variables or a .env file for LLM API keys, ticketing/CRM API tokens, and database connection strings (do not commit secrets).

step_by_step.title: Load or generate workloads
actions: If using real data: export historical tickets from your ticketing system including ticket_id, creation time, first response time, status history, agent IDs, channel, tags, free-text fields, and any CSAT scores.
Run provided ETL scripts to normalize and anonymize ticket data into the repository's expected schema (e.g., tickets.parquet or tickets.jsonl).
If using synthetic data: run the included synthetic ticket generator script to create a corpus of tickets across defined issue categories and channels.
Split the dataset into tuning, validation, and holdout subsets using the provided scripts.

step_by_step.title: Index the knowledge base
actions: Export your existing KB articles or use the synthetic KB from the repository.
Run the indexing script to embed documents into the configured vector store, generating embeddings and metadata (category, product area, version).
Verify that retrieval works by running test queries and manually inspecting top-k results.

step_by_step.title: Configure and test agents offline
actions: Edit prompt templates and policy configuration files for triage, knowledge, resolver, and quality-review agents to reflect your domain.
Run the offline simulation script on the tuning subset of tickets to generate proposed classifications and responses without sending any messages.
Review a random sample of agent outputs, particularly for high-risk categories, using provided Jupyter notebooks or CLI tools.
Iterate on prompts and policy thresholds until offline quality and safety criteria are met.
Run the simulation on the holdout subset to confirm generalization.

step_by_step.title: Deploy orchestration and integrations
actions: Deploy the orchestration service (REST API or message-driven worker) to your chosen environment (e.g., Kubernetes, Docker Compose).
Set up webhooks or polling from the ticketing system to send new ticket events to the orchestration endpoint.
Configure the ticketing system to add experiment metadata (arm assignment, experiment_id) to each ticket via triggers or apps.
Implement status update and comment-posting callbacks from the orchestration service back into the ticketing system.

step_by_step.title: Run a shadow-mode test in production
actions: Enable the orchestration service in 'shadow' mode where agentic decisions are computed and logged but not applied to live tickets.
Run shadow mode for at least several days to verify stability, latency, and logging.
Compare agentic proposed responses with actual human responses for a sampled set of tickets.
Confirm that guardrails correctly flag or block risky cases.

step_by_step.title: Start limited live A/B experiment (Phase 1)
actions: Enable random assignment of a small fraction of new tickets (e.g., 10%) to the treatment path with agentic handling; leave the rest as control.
Configure the treatment path so that all agentic responses require human approval before sending, at least during initial days.
Monitor key safety metrics daily (policy violations, customer complaints) and technical metrics (failure rates, latency).
If no material issues are detected, gradually enable auto-send for clearly low-risk categories (e.g., simple FAQs) under quality-review oversight.

step_by_step.title: Scale experiment to main measurement window (Phase 2)
actions: Increase treatment allocation to 30–50% of incoming tickets, maintaining stratified randomization.
Freeze agent configuration (prompts, model versions, thresholds) at the start of this phase.
Run the experiment for at least 2–4 weeks or until the pre-computed sample size requirement is reached in both arms.
Ensure continuous monitoring and incident response; any major configuration change must be timestamped and documented.

step_by_step.title: Collect and analyze results
actions: Export experiment logs (ticket-level with arm assignment, timestamps, metrics, and CSAT responses) to the analysis database or files.
Run the provided analysis scripts or notebooks to compute metrics per arm, perform significance tests, and visualize distributions.
Segment results by channel, customer tier, and issue category to understand where agents help or hurt most.
Document findings in the format specified by the evidence_schema, including confidence intervals and notable qualitative observations.

step_by_step.title: Decide on rollout and iterate
actions: Compare results against success_criteria; identify which ticket segments meet thresholds for broader agentic adoption.
Plan a phased rollout where low-risk segments move to higher agent coverage, while higher-risk segments remain human-led with agent assistance.
Update financial models (cost per ticket, OPEX projections) using measured metrics.
Capture lessons learned and update guardrails, training, and runbooks accordingly.

evidence_schema.description: Structured format for capturing the outcomes, configuration, and context of the experiment so that others can interpret and replicate it.

experiment_metadata.organization_id: string or null; anonymized org identifier if shared externally
experiment_metadata.config_git_commit: string; Git commit hash of configuration and prompt set used during the experiment window

configuration_snapshot.treatment_allocation: float; fraction of tickets assigned to treatment during live phases
configuration_snapshot.auto_send_enabled: boolean; whether agents were allowed to auto-send replies without human approval
configuration_snapshot.auto_send_scope: array of strings; issue categories/channels eligible for auto-send
configuration_snapshot.guardrail_policies: object; summarized configuration of high-risk rules (e.g., max_refund_amount, restricted_topics)
configuration_snapshot.agent_roles_enabled: array of strings; which agents (triage, knowledge, resolver, quality_review) were active

staffing_context.num_l1_agents: integer; average concurrent L1 agents during experiment
staffing_context.num_l2_agents: integer; average concurrent L2 agents during experiment

qualitative_observations.agent_failure_modes_examples: array of case descriptions highlighting notable agent errors or unexpected behaviors.
qualitative_observations.human_feedback_summary: text summary of agent and supervisor qualitative feedback during the experiment.
qualitative_observations.customer_feedback_snippets: array of anonymized customer comments related to support quality and response content.
qualitative_observations.operational_lessons_learned: text; key takeaways for future iterations and for other organizations attempting similar experiments.

conclusion.summary: short text synopsis of whether the experiment supports the hypothesis and under what constraints or caveats.
conclusion.recommended_next_steps: text; suggested rollout plan, further experiments (e.g., by segment), and any governance updates.
